import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Maximal run lengths in the second MSB of Tribonacci numbers $T(n)$

The Tribonacci numbers $T_n$ (A000073).
$T_0=0, T_1=0, T_2=1$, and $T_n = T_{n-1} + T_{n-2} + T_{n-3}$ for $n \ge 3$.

Second most significant bit of the tribonacci number A000073(n).
This is formalized by extracting the bit at position $\lfloor \log_2 T_n \rfloor - 1$.

*References:*
- [A271591](https://oeis.org/A271591)
- [arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763) *Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search* by George Tsoukalas et al.
- [A000073](https://oeis.org/A000073)
-/

namespace OeisA271591


open Nat

/--
The Tribonacci numbers $T_n$ (A000073).
$T_0=0, T_1=0, T_2=1$, and $T_n = T_{n-1} + T_{n-2} + T_{n-3}$ for $n \ge 3$.
-/
def tribonacci (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  match n with
  | 0 => 0
  | 1 => 0
  | 2 => 1
  | n + 3 => (tribonacci (n + 2)) + (tribonacci (n + 1)) + (tribonacci n)

/--
Second most significant bit of the tribonacci number A000073(n).
This is formalized by extracting the bit at position $\lfloor \log_2 T_n \rfloor - 1$.
-/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  let T := tribonacci n
  -- The index of the MSB is T.log2. The index of the second MSB is T.log2 - 1.
  if T ≤ 1 then
    0
  else
    let j_smsb : ℕ := T.log2 - 1
    if T.testBit j_smsb then 1 else 0

def IsMaximalRun (v : ℕ) (n L : ℕ) : Prop :=
  n ≥ 2 ∧ L ≥ 1 ∧
  -- The run consists of L consecutive $v$'s starting at n
  (∀ i : ℕ, i < L → a (n + i) = v) ∧
  -- The run is not followed by $v$
  (a (n + L) ≠ v) ∧
  -- The run is not preceded by $v$
  (a (n - 1) ≠ v)


@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_4 : a 4 = 0 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_5 : a 5 = 0 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_6 : a 6 = 1 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_7 : a 7 = 1 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_8 : a 8 = 1 := by rfl


/--
It is conjectured that after the first two 0's, the number of consecutive 0's is only 4 or 5, and the number of consecutive 1's is only 3 or 4 (tested up to $n = 10^4$).

A formal proof has been found with the methods described in
[arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/a32396489dcb8f86c3549b93aa358ac6a10a3a1f/FormalConjectures/OEIS/271591.wip.lean#L497"]
theorem maximal_run_lengths : (∀ n L, IsMaximalRun 0 n L → (L = 4 ∨ L = 5)) ∧
    (∀ n L, IsMaximalRun 1 n L → (L = 3 ∨ L = 4)) := by
    sorry

end OeisA271591

reformulations.difference: OEIS starts the sequence at n = 4 and explicitly exempts its initial two zeros. Lean extends a to smaller natural indices by zero and uses IsMaximalRun with n ≥ 2 and unequal neighboring terms, without an explicit initial-run exception.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Lean has a(0) = ⋯ = a(5) = 0 and a(6) = 1, so every IsMaximalRun starts at n ≥ 6. Define SourceRun as a maximal run in the official sequence starting at index 4, allowing a run to start at that left endpoint. The scratch file proves IsMaximalRun v n L ↔ SourceRun v n L ∧ n ≠ 4, and SourceRun 1 n L ↔ IsMaximalRun 1 n L. The only excluded source run is the initial zero run at n = 4 of length 2. Thus the theorem states exactly the source's run-length restrictions. Review271591.source_statement_iff proves the full equivalence without using the sorry-backed conjecture.

sources_consulted: https://arxiv.org/e-print/2605.22763 — v2 LaTeX, particularly the OEIS discussion in Section 2
https://arxiv.org/e-print/2608.11941 — v2 LaTeX, Appendix A entry for A271591

Computation matched all 3,001 A000073 b-file entries and all 9,997 A271591 entries. All 2,415 completed noninitial runs through n = 10,000 had the stated lengths. The current OEIS comment records the proof on May 28, 2026, agreeing with research solved. The cited proof was inspected and kernel-checked in a scratch copy after updating its import path and replacing one version-sensitive auxiliary proof with a deduction from its already-proved induction lemma. ProofComparison.proof_matches_current establishes the committed statement with axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] only. Successful experiments are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean and /workspace/review/proof-comparison.lean. The reviewed file remains byte-identical to the committed version.
